Real-time toggle: when disabled, the attribute learning bonus feature is completely inactive (values are kept but not applied)

Level cap for Vigor skills (One Handed / Two Handed / Polearm)

Level cap for Social skills (Charm / Leadership / Trade)
Level cap for Intelligence skills (Steward / Medicine / Engineering)
Prevent AI lords from recruiting non-main-hero clan parties into armies
Prevent non-main-hero clan parties from donating troops to garrisons
Make non-player clan leaders attempt to create armies to test the blocking effect
In the prisoner tab of the party screen, mark rulers/lords/mercenary leaders with their identity
In the encyclopedia clan list, add "In Exile / Not in Exile" options to the Status filter group (no kingdom, no fiefs, not rebel/bandit/minor faction, excluding player clan)
Enable/disable the troop restoration feature after releasing lords
Days needed to restore troops after release
Restored troops as a ratio of the party size limit (0 = disabled)
Gold given to the lord per troop (0 = no gold)
Food given to the lord per troop to prevent starvation (0 = no food)
Abandon restoration if the lord still has no party after this many days
Enable/disable the territory loss compensation feature
Party size limit increase per lost town (before diminishing)
Party size limit increase per lost castle (before diminishing)
Diminishing multiplier for consecutive territory losses (1.0 = linear)
Maximum cumulative compensation a kingdom can accumulate
After holding a settlement for this many days, it counts as home territory and no longer offsets compensation (0 = disabled, 84 = one year)
After a lost settlement stays lost for this many days, it counts as foreign territory and no longer participates in compensation (0 = disabled, 84 = one year)
Only apply to vassal clans (excluding mercenaries)
Maximum number of ships the player can field simultaneously in naval battles/coastal raids (at least 3, at most 8)
Main Menu Custom Battle: Land First

Open the land (non-naval) battle configuration first when entering Custom Battle from the main menu. Warsail DLC makes the naval configuration the default entry; enabling this restores land battle first (the switch button still cycles between both modes)
Show a toast notification in the center of the screen when a clan member becomes available after being released/escaping captivity
Display lord troop restoration debug logs in the bottom-left corner of the screen to troubleshoot restoration logic
Display territory loss compensation debug logs in the bottom-left corner of the screen to troubleshoot compensation calculations and UI refresh
Display companion availability reminder debug logs in the bottom-left corner of the screen
In battle, press , to force-zero ammunition of 5% of ranged soldiers to test the formation 9 transfer logic
Show a red circle under the player and a yellow point ahead (debugging)
Display dated-save logs in the bottom-left corner of the screen (new save names, save results, pruned old saves) to troubleshoot naming and rotation logic
When the player is king, prevent AI lords from automatically proposing war declarations
Fiefs conquered personally by the player are always included in the fief assignment vote
When attacking, siege engines prioritize enemy ranged siege engines

When the player starts a siege first (alone or leading their own army), the siege command stays with the player — a friendly army joining later cannot take it over. When disabled, restores vanilla behavior (the highest-ranking leader present, e.g. a king or an army leader, takes command)
Pure infantry/ranged squads auto-crouch when holding still (first rank of line formations / front half of ranged / all ranged in loose formations)
Front-rank soldiers raise shields upward instead of downward while crouching
Move banner bearers from the left front to the middle of the last rank
Ranged soldiers with depleted ammunition are auto-moved to formation 9 and return when ammo is restored
Reverse the sort cycle when clicking scoreboard column headers: default → descending → ascending
No AI Takeover on Player Death

After the player character dies, prevent the system from forcing full AI command of the player's party; the party keeps executing the last orders given before the player's death (the vanilla order UI is still closed after death, so no further manual orders can be issued). When disabled, restores vanilla: full AI takeover on death

Fix the vanilla formation arrangement convergence defect: shielded (or polearm-bracing) units keep bubbling forward until the column stabilizes, and cross-column gap filling skips full ranks instead of aborting the whole arrangement, ensuring the front rank is fully shielded whenever shield units are available (vanilla can leave a disordered mix of non-shield front rank + shield second rank)
Mounted couch lance (passive attack) hits on unmounted infantry/ranged units always knock them down (symmetric for both sides; negated by blocking)
Normal mounted polearm thrusts hitting unmounted infantry/ranged units always knock them down (symmetric for both sides; negated by blocking)

Minimum relative speed required to trigger guaranteed knockdown on a mounted polearm thrust (length of the velocity difference vector between attacker and target, same unit as game speed). Default 2.0 prevents stationary thrusts from knocking down; 0 removes the speed requirement
Damage bonus applied when a mounted polearm thrust triggers guaranteed knockdown (default 0.3 = +30%). 0 means no damage bonus

Active when game setting "Unit Spawn Priority = High Tier First": schedules spawn pacing by the four ratio weights below (infantry/archer/cavalry/horse archer), while within a troop type units still spawn highest tier first, preventing high-tier troops from monopolizing all spawn slots. When disabled, reverts to vanilla high-tier-first logic
Infantry spawn quota weight (relative value; higher = more frequent; 0 = infantry never spawns; total of all four is recommended to be 100)
Archer spawn quota weight (relative value; higher = more frequent; 0 = archers never spawn; total of all four is recommended to be 100)
Cavalry spawn quota weight (relative value; higher = more frequent; 0 = cavalry never spawns; total of all four is recommended to be 100)
Horse archer spawn quota weight (relative value; higher = more frequent; 0 = horse archers never spawn; total of all four is recommended to be 100)
Enable NPC Clan Party Limit Bonus
Add extra parties on top of the vanilla party limit for all AI lord clans (only affects daily AI dispatch, not the player clan)
Extra parties added on top of the vanilla party limit for all NPC lord clans (default +2: Tier 0-2 clans from 1 to 3 parties, Tier 3-4 from 2 to 4, Tier 5-6 from 3 to 5; 0 disables the bonus)
Real-time toggle: when disabled, the recruitment refill rate multiplier has no effect (notables keep vanilla daily refill)

Multiplier for the daily chance of town/village notables refilling recruits (1.0 = vanilla, 2.0 = expected doubling; deeper slots have lower vanilla rates and are scaled proportionally; above 1.9 the first slots will always refill, but upgrades still need separate acceleration)
Real-time toggle: when disabled, the volunteer upgrade rate multiplier has no effect (keeps vanilla extremely low upgrade chance)

Multiplier for the daily upgrade chance of troops owned by town/village notables (1.0 = vanilla; vanilla chance = log2(influence/level)*0.01, e.g. a level-2 notable with 30 influence has ~5% daily upgrade chance; a 10x multiplier gives ~50%)

After joining an existing friendly battle on the campaign map (whether friendlies attack or defend), the encounter menu always offers a "Leave" option to withdraw with your party at any time; battles you started yourself (defending/attacking sieges) keep vanilla rules

Quick save and auto save use "date and time of saving" as names (save_qu_/save_au_ prefixes), each campaign rotates its own pool; when full, the oldest save of that campaign is pruned after a new save succeeds. Save As and ironman keep vanilla logic. When disabled, fully reverts to vanilla naming (saveNNN / saveauto1-3); already-created dated saves are not auto-deleted

Maximum files per campaign in the rotation pool for dated saves (auto + quick): when the pool of a campaign is full, the next quick/auto save first saves the new file successfully, then prunes the oldest by time; saves of different campaigns never prune each other (1-50, default 10)

Every 6 in-game hours, surplus player-clan towns dispatch transport parties converted from garrisons to starving player-clan towns/castles, adding/subtracting town food values directly (bypassing market consumption)
Player-clan towns/castles with food below this value are listed as starving and await support from other towns (town cap 300, castle cap 450)
Player-clan towns only dispatch transport parties when their food is above this value (dispatched food never takes the town below this value)
Player-clan towns only dispatch transport parties when garrison size is above this value (vanilla minimum garrison: town 125 / castle 75)
Number of soldiers converted from garrison per transport party (half high-tier/half low-tier randomly picked; battle losses are permanent, survivors return to garrison on return)

Abstract support food carried per soldier: total support food = transport party size × this value, deducted from source town food on departure and added to target town food on arrival (not via market)
Physical grain carried per soldier (into party inventory, only for the transport party's own consumption en route, not interchangeable with support food; leftovers destroyed on delivery/return)
Maximum number of transport parties the same starving town/castle can accept support from at the same time
Maximum number of transport parties the same surplus town can dispatch at the same time
Display food transport dispatch/delivery/exception logs in the bottom-left corner of the screen (dispatch, delivery, refund, destroyed, etc.)
Show food transport parties on the campaign map globally, like your clan's armies, regardless of distance or fog of war

Remove the 28-day survival countdown extinction mechanic for landless exiled clans (clans wandering after their kingdom falls), letting them persist forever until joining another kingdom or gaining land. When disabled, restores vanilla countdown extinction

The menu of fully raided (devastated) villages offers a "Fund Reconstruction" option: pay 10000 denars and the village rebuilds automatically in 3 days (returns to normal operation and rewards all notables with 15~20 relation). When disabled, the menu option is hidden; ongoing paid rebuilds are unaffected and still complete on time
Removing a hero prisoner directly in the party screen (dragging them out of the party roster) now grants the same +4 relation as releasing them through dialogue, following the vanilla relation flow

Cap the number of simultaneously visible kill feed entries in battle (top-right corner); when exceeded, the oldest entry is removed immediately so a mass casualty pileup never stretches the feed off-screen
Maximum number of kill feed entries displayed at the same time (entries beyond this are removed oldest-first; default 6 keeps the top-right feed compact)

Gradually shrink the text of older kill feed entries once the on-screen entry count exceeds the threshold below (newest stays full size, oldest shrinks down to the minimum scale), creating a clear visual hierarchy
Entries beyond this on-screen count start shrinking (e.g. 4 means the 5th+ entry shrinks; oldest shrinks most)
Smallest font scale applied to the oldest kill feed entry (0.7 = 70% of the normal font size; newer entries interpolate between this and 100%)

Overhaul the auto-resolve (simulate battle) calculation: troops accumulate damage with individual HP instead of dying instantly, hit damage comes from the striker's actual weapon (4x4 class-vs-class priority table), armor reduces damage with the vanilla formula, shield-bearers can block, and lopsided battles get extra rounds to finish. When disabled, all auto-resolve logic reverts to vanilla
Apply to AI vs AI Battles
Apply the rebalanced logic to battles between AI parties on the campaign map. When disabled, only player-simulated battles (auto-resolve) are affected

Shorten the simulation interval between battle rounds for AI vs AI battles on the campaign map (default 1.0 = battles between AI parties resolve at normal speed). Hit damage, armor and weapon formulas are unchanged; player-simulated auto-resolve is never affected

Apply the vanilla damage-reduction formula to the struck troop's armor (random hit location: head / arm / leg / torso): raw damage is reduced by 50/(50+armor) then further reduced by the armor value scaled by damage type (cut -50%, pierce -33%, blunt -20%), while a blunt-factor portion (blunt 60% / cut 10%) ignores armor entirely. When disabled, armor is ignored in auto-resolve
Chance that an attack against a shield-bearing infantry/cavalry troop is blocked by the shield, dealing no damage (default 0.1 = 10%). Ranged troops (archers/horse archers) never get shield blocks

Chance that an infantry/cavalry troop carrying a javelin throws it instead of attacking in melee (default 0.05 = 5%). A troop carrying only javelins always throws (100%) and never fights unarmed. Ranged troops never use javelins
Hit chance for ranged attacks (bows/crossbows/slings and thrown javelins) in auto-resolve (default 0.8 = 80%). A miss deals no damage this hit

Cap the attack-frequency ratio between the two sides in auto-resolve. Attack frequency scales with (force ratio)^0.6; with the default cap of 2.0 the frequency ratio never exceeds 2^0.6 ≈ 1.52, so a bigger army attacks at most ~1.5x more often no matter how lopsided the battle gets. Set to 1 to remove the cap

Write a full CSV log of every player-simulated auto-resolve battle for later analysis (battle summary, per-round stats, per-hit weapon/armor/damage details, and every casualty event). Files are saved to '<game root>\MutliLittleFixes_AutoResolveLogs\<timestamp>\' with UTF-8 BOM encoding and can be opened directly in Excel/WPS. Only battles simulated by the player are logged; AI vs AI battles are never recorded
Display auto-resolve rebalance debug logs (per-hit HP changes, data rebuilds, errors) in the bottom-left corner of the screen
